name: claude-agent-scaffolding
description: Personal plugin marketplace for agent-assisted development: dual-repo workspace bootstrap, spec-driven and skeleton-first delivery lifecycles, anti-sycophancy design critique, strict code-quality and architecture review, configuration security auditing, and decision-making mentor surfaces. Described by capability rather than by plugin name, so it does not go stale as plugins land.

plugins.name: workspace-init
plugins.description: Bootstrap a dual-repo workspace (AI workspace + canonical) with pairing manifest and AI-trace commit-msg filter. Run-once plugin; first in the scaffolding chain. 2 skills (initializing-dual-repo-workspace, pairing-canonical-repo), 2 slash commands (/init-workspace, /pair-workspace via $ARGUMENTS bridge). Pairing manifest schema v1.0 at <ai-workspace>/.workspace/pairing.json. commit-msg hook filters AI-trace lines with baked AI workspace path. Scenario A migration (--pair-with). 145 tests across 10 suites.

plugins.name: ai-mentor
plugins.description: Decision-making mentor. Four skills auto-invoke on natural-language triggers: grill-me (one-question-at-a-time plan interrogation with CORE posture + 4 cognitive-discipline escape valves), council (5-persona multi-angle idea validation, Karpathy LLM Council pattern with codebase-aware Historian), eli10 (repeatable simplification), fool (sticky beginner's-mind mode). Skill-first; no hooks, no state.

plugins.name: scaffold-onboard
plugins.description: Project onboarding (v0.2 skill-first retrofit). 7 skills auto-invoke on natural-language triggers: onboarding-project (10-phase MASTER-SPEC.md authoring), scaffolding-memory-bank (11-file bank + Karpathy-opt-in CLAUDE.md), scaffolding-governance-docs (5/14 docs), planning-project-roadmap (R1: Phase→Sprint→VS hierarchy → ROADMAP.md with 3-timelines framing + 5 re-run modes), authoring-machine-checkable-rules (R2: HTML-sentinel mcrule DSL, 4 rule types, warn-and-skip extensibility), authoring-vertical-slice-demo (R3: auto:/user: grammar with literal U+2192 arrow), validating-master-spec. 4 slash commands wrap the skills via $ARGUMENTS bridge. Manifest-aware routing for dual-repo workspaces (single-repo fallback preserved). Tier 0 marker protocol coordinates with scaffold-dev. Critic invocation via filesystem-probe; paired-release with architect-critic v0.2.

plugins.name: scaffold-dev
plugins.description: Sprint-driven orchestrator-implementer workflow for dual-repo workspaces. 13 skills, 7 slash commands, custom implementer-agent subagent type via Task tool, handoff escape valve. Composes with workspace-init (manifest), scaffold-onboard (R1/R2/R3 contract), architect-critic (filesystem probe + critiquing-spec), ai-mentor (grill-me at 3 gates). Replaces scaffold v1.0.0.

plugins.name: scaffold
plugins.description: DEPRECATED — replaced by scaffold-dev v0.1.0. Project-level workflow plugin. Bootstrap or audit any repo, run slice-driven 5-phase workflow (spec → contract → scaffold → implement → verify), manage living governance (ADRs, CHANGELOG, runbooks), and search a per-repo memory bank via Ollama-backed semantic recall (FTS5 fallback). Worktree-safe: state lives outside the working tree so parallel branches inherit/fork cleanly. 18 slash commands + 10 MCP tools.

plugins.name: architect-critic
plugins.description: Anti-sycophancy reviewer (v0.2 skill-first). 4 skills auto-invoke on natural-language triggers: critiquing-spec (audit + sequential rebuttal with T=4 concession scoring), reviewing-critique-history, listing-principles, promoting-principle. Ships ghost-notes (Wald survivor-bias) + CORE protocol (Curiosity/Objectivity/Reassurance/Empathy) as default principles. Full auto-promotion: vote-recurrence T=4 + instinct N=3 consecutive + 30/90-day suppression. Codex 0.125+ adversarial fresh-frame at close-depth. Standalone-invocable; consumer plugins (scaffold-onboard v0.2+, scaffold-dev v0.1+) invoke skills in-conversation (no file IPC).

plugins.name: claude-security-audit
plugins.description: Static-analysis security audit for Claude Code project configurations and enabled plugins. 28 rules across 7 aspects: secrets (Anthropic/OpenAI/GitHub/AWS keys, JWTs, env-var leaks, base64 blobs), permissions (broad-allow, missing-deny, settings.local divergence, PERM-005 schema-typo validation, dangerous combos), hooks (curl|bash, rm -rf, unbounded eval, network exfiltration), MCP (untrusted endpoints, missing auth, env-var leaks), CLAUDE.md (plaintext secrets, internal markers), prompt-injection in agents/commands (common patterns; AST is v0.2), marketplace (untrusted sources, malformed manifest). Two-flag auto-fix (T2-H) gated on `RULE_AUTO_FIXABLE` + `RULE_MECHANICALLY_FIXABLE` with 5-layer defense-in-depth (rule re-validation, target re-resolution, symlink refusal, path-traversal refusal, atomic state log). Durable `finding_uid` (T2-I) survives whitespace/line-drift edits; baseline diff tags NEW vs PERSISTED. Self-tamper detection (T1-F) on state.json + suppressions.json. Critical-cannot-suppress + 60s race-window refusal. Zero ambient surface by default — SessionStart reminder ships as opt-in file (T1-C). Inspired by AgentShield in Everything Claude Code (Mustafa, 2026; MIT) — independent MIT implementation tailored to composable plugin marketplaces.

plugins.name: ossify
plugins.description: Skeleton-first replacement lifecycle for scaffold-onboard + scaffold-dev. Install one lifecycle or the other, not both. workspace-init is optional as of 1.3.0: /ossify:start and /ossify:adopt author .ossify/topology.json themselves, reading a workspace-init pairing.json as a translated fallback only when one exists. 9 native skills (start, adopt, plan-release, plan-spine, doctor, work-item, close, challenge, wayfinder), 13 slash commands, and an implementer subagent. Self-sufficient since 1.1.0: the grill and the adversarial critic ship in-tree as /ossify:challenge, with a configurable external adversary. /ossify:start does the pre-code spec-core onboarding and /ossify:adopt onboards a project that already has code (five fail-closed gates, six conversions, Release 0 closed retroactively); /ossify:plan-release opens a release and /ossify:plan-spine lays out its skeleton; /ossify:run-spine drives a planned spine round by round, and since 1.8.0 accepts an optional --external-executor flag that hands each round's work items to a caller-supplied, provider-neutral in-session procedure (one request record out per item, one result record back) instead of dispatching the nested implementer subagent — the no-flag command is unchanged; /ossify:close runs the close ceremony with memory harvest; /ossify:doctor diagnoses state, spec, rules, interop, budgets and plugin provenance. /ossify:wayfinder (new at 1.2.0) charts a question into decision tickets on the issue tracker and works an existing map's frontier one ticket per session. The any-repo utilities /ossify:handoff, /ossify:handoff-resume, /ossify:work-pr (review-fix-merge loop) and /ossify:wayfinder run standalone on any gh repo.

plugins.name: code-judo
plugins.description: Strict quality review and architecture deepening. 4 prose skills, 4 slash commands, no runtime library. deep-review is a human-invoked maintainability audit of a diff or branch — the code-judo ambition standard (restructurings that delete complexity rather than rearrange it), the 1000-line rule with its waiver path, spaghetti-growth suspicion, wrapper/cast/boundary rules, a 7-tier prioritized output order, and a categorical approval bar with 6 presumptive blockers. It produces one report and one disposition pass and never re-reviews its own fixes; its verdict is advisory, never a merge gate. deepen-architecture scans a codebase for shallow modules using the deletion test, writes a single HTML report to the OS temp dir with before/after diagrams and Strong/Worth-exploring/Speculative badges, opens it in the browser, and grills through the candidate you pick. codebase-design ships the deep-module vocabulary (module, interface, depth, seam, adapter, leverage, locality), the four dependency categories, seam discipline, and design-it-twice. domain-modeling keeps the CONTEXT.md glossary where nothing else owns the project's vocabulary, and composes ADRs without filing them — the ADR directory is a numbered sequence and it leaves that to whichever plugin owns it. No hard cross-plugin dependencies: the grilling step resolves softly to ossify:challenge, then ai-mentor:grill-me, then an in-plugin protocol. Adapted from Cursor's thermo-nuclear code-quality review and Matt Pocock's improve-codebase-architecture.

plugins.name: orca-crew
plugins.description: The orchestrator/worker session model over Orca orchestration. An orchestrator session (claude on Fable, or claude-sol) keeps its context for decisions and dispatches everything else to GLM sessions launched by alias: claude-glm or claude-glm-flash implement by complexity class, one claude-glm-flash session runs /code-review once per PR, the retained implementer works GitHub threads to zero, merge only on the operator's word. A session budget caps each work item at one implementer and one verifier. Since 0.3.0, a spine planned in that same session runs in three layers: the orchestrator ratifies one implementer/verifier profile per work item into an orca-execution/v1 sidecar and starts one spine session; that session creates a child Run and owns both item terminals per item; each item gets a fresh pair at its exact ratified command, model and effort. Nested worker depth 2 is required with no fallback, no inherited-runtime subagent runs in that path, and the reviewer is chosen only when the spine's PR reaches review. Since 0.4.0 the spine-session seat is a ratified sidecar block, the first verifier failure blocks and asks, the close and every PR loop run in fresh sessions the top dispatches, and the record pass is single and conditional. Defers every other Orca command to the Orca binary's own guide. No lib, no hooks, no state.
